newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore banks seen maintaining strong growth.
newsitem.headline: Singapore banks seen maintaining strong growth.

text.p: Singapore's four major banks should see strong double digit earnings growth this year despite the country's economic slowdown, banking analysts said on Thursday.

In the reporting season just ended, the Big Four -- OCBC Bank, United Overseas Bank, DBS Bank and Overseas Union Bank -- posted a higher than expected 15 percent rise in combined net profit for 1996 to Singapore $2.4 billion (US$1.7 billion).
Banking analysts said they expected the Big Four to maintain their mid-teens earnings growth in 1997.
"We still like the banks. There aren't that many big cap stocks in Singapore which are liquid and have such good growth," said Seah Hiang Hong, investment analyst with Kim Eng Securities.
Seah said with the exception of DBS Bank, the banks had good regional exposure which would continue the soften the impact of the slowdown in Singapore's economy.
Heath McIntyre, analyst with HSBC James Capel, agreed. "Overseas operations will continue to buffer earnings from the domestic side," he said.
OCBC, OUB and UOB have a strong overseas networks, especially in Malaysia. Analysts said they estimated the overseas operations contributed between 25 to 30 percent of their earnings.
UOB's earnings in particular were boosted strongly by its Malaysian operations, which contributed S$131 million to group net profit of S$715.5 million in 1996.
"I expect OUB, OCBC and UOB to continue to rely quite a bit on their overseas contributions for growth," said a banking analyst with SocGen Crosby Securities.
Analysts said the slowdown in the domestic economy would, however, have an impact, especially in terms of loans growth.
"I expect loans growth for the Big Four to slow to 16 percent this year from 20 percent in 1996," said the SocGen Crosby analyst.
Interest margins for local banks could also come under pressure later in the year, especially if Singapore interbank rates rise under pressure from higher U.S. interest rates, the analysts said.
OCBC Bank remained a clear favourite after surprising analysts with a 17 percent jump in 1996 earnings to S$708.9 million.
"OCBC was certainly the most impressive. It continues to be our top pick for the sector," said McIntyre.
The analysts also said they expected DBS Bank to put in a better performance this year as it begins to reap the benefit of a big push into the housing loan market.
"DBS should see higher interest spreads this year. They went after the housing loan market aggressively about three years ago," said Seah.
